title: Private VPC backplane heartbeat & artifact handoff criteria for zero-egress sites
creator: Rohan Mehta
description: PRD fragment: define deterministic acceptance criteria for the VPC backplane heartbeat, operator orchestration, and offline artifact handoff used by private (zero/limited-egress) deployments. Goal: ensure upgrades and operator actions can be performed safely in environments that disallow continuous outbound connections. This ticket captures requirements, scope decision points, test harnesses, and operational playbook hooks required for delivery.
scope_changes: Initial PRD included a full operator rework; scoped down to heartbeat + artifact handoff protocol and canary rollout signals to limit delivery risk.
Excluded: UI console changes and billing/usage reporting for mirrors; these will be tracked separately.
Added: explicit checksum and provenance validation for artifacts during handoff after security review feedback (2025-02-20).
acceptance_criteria: Heartbeat contract: operator agent in customer VPC must send or be able to receive a signed heartbeat record once per configured heartbeat interval (default 15m) when egress window is available; platform must tolerate heartbeat gaps up to 3x interval with defined 'degraded' state visible in Console.

Offline artifact handoff: a staged artifact bundle (images + signatures + manifest) can be delivered via customer-provided mirror endpoint or removable media; the agent must validate SHA256 checksums and signed manifest before installation.

Upgrade orchestration: control-plane orchestrated canary must support a three-way state: pending, staged, committed. In zero-egress sites the control plane must mark 'staged' after successful offline handoff and allow operator-triggered commit only after local health checks pass.

No implicit external pull: in zero-egress mode, operator or installer SHALL NOT attempt to directly pull from public registries or Redwood cloud; any attempt is logged and fails the upgrade acceptance test.

Rollback criteria: if post-commit health probes fail 2 consecutive windows (configurable, default 10m), platform must provide automated rollback to previous image within operator permissions and surface a rollback runbook with reason codes.

KMS/key rotation: artifact manifests signed with customer or Redwood key; rotation must verify backwards compatibility for last two keys. Acceptance requires a documented rotation test in the offline handoff harness.

Telemetry gating: minimal telemetry (status pings, error codes, artifact IDs) may be emitted during configured egress window; acceptance requires opt-in consent per customer contract and ability to buffer 14 days locally for scheduled upload.

Canary verification: staged canary must run smoke prompts and sample inference workload (configurable token budget) locally; results compared to baseline within tolerated delta (quantified in PRD) before commit.
Operator RBAC: only identities with operator-level RBAC can trigger commit/rollback; acceptance includes automated policy test in the deployment harness.
Test harness: provide an offline test suite that simulates mirror handoff, heartbeat loss, staggered commit, and rollback; tests must pass in CI with synthetic private-vpc fixtures prior to release.
Audit logging: handoff, heartbeat anomalies, and commit/rollback events must be recorded locally and exported on next allowed egress; acceptance requires log schema and example records in docs.
Security sign-off: security_review_required = true and sign-off must be attached to the release when shipping private-2025.03 features.

Operator agent health: after commit, agent must report node-level SLO metrics (CPU, GPU memory, kv-cache hit rate) for at least 72 hours without full egress; acceptance requires a sample 72h report generated by harness.

Mirror failure fallback: if mirror handoff fails and no alternative mirrored artifact is available within configured retry window, system must provide documented emergency patch procedure (manual operator instructions) with zero-privilege escalation path.

Backward compatibility: Private clusters running runtime <= 1.16 must be able to opt into the new handshake protocol; acceptance includes compatibility matrix and automated upgrade simulation from 1.15/1.16 in staging.

Operator observability hooks: Console displays 'handoff readiness' and 'staged commit' states for private clusters in the deployments page; acceptance requires a mock Console screenshot and dataset used by UI team for implementation.
